title: security: daemon /ws and /mcp accept browser-origin WebSocket upgrades, and WSL agent mode binds them on every interface
description:
Filed at the human's direction on 2026-10-30 (governor REPL, priority HIGH), from worker-0062feec's finding on CQ-RF05 (task-b439d7fb, comment-4bef8984). Confirmed by the governor against the live daemon.

Problem class: an unauthenticated local control channel that is reachable from untrusted origins.
1. packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts builds its WebSocket server with no verifyClient, and the daemon source has no Origin handling at all. A WebSocket upgrade that a browser makes on behalf of any web page is accepted on /ws and /mcp; only /runner authenticates. Browsers do not apply CORS to WebSocket upgrades. The server must check Origin itself.
2. In WSL agent mode (JetBrains "Run Agents in WSL"), MoeDaemonSupervisor spawns the daemon with --host 0.0.0.0. The live daemon was confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:9876 on 2026-10-30. That puts the same unauthenticated endpoints on every host interface, not just the WSL virtual network, and only Windows Firewall stands between them and the LAN.

Why it matters: /mcp drives the board (create tasks, set status, chat), and agents act on task contents. Keep this row's own text at the level of the problem class. Do not write exploit steps into task fields or chat, because .moe/tasks is committed and pushed.

Wanted:
- Refuse browser-originated upgrades on /ws and /mcp: a present Origin header that is not explicitly allowed is rejected. The Moe clients (moe-proxy, the JetBrains plugin, the VS Code extension, the wrapper RPC helper) must keep working; check which of them send an Origin header, if any.
- In WSL agent mode, bind only to the interface WSL agents actually use (the WSL virtual adapter or its gateway address), not 0.0.0.0, while WSL agents still reach the daemon the way moe-agent.sh discovers it (loopback, then the WSL gateway).
- JetBrains first (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt), then VS Code parity.
- Coordinate with CQ-RF05's re-decision (task-b439d7fb), which owns the threat-model write-up. This row owns the code fix.
definitionOfDone: A WebSocket upgrade to /ws or /mcp that carries a browser Origin header outside the allowed set is refused before any message is processed. moe-proxy, the JetBrains plugin client, the VS Code extension and the wrapper RPC path still connect. Daemon tests cover a refused browser origin, an absent Origin, and each real client's actual handshake.

In WSL agent mode the daemon no longer listens on 0.0.0.0. It binds the WSL-facing interface (or another bound host that a test pins), and a WSL seat still reaches /health and /mcp through moe-agent.sh's discovery. Tests cover both the JetBrains supervisor argv and the daemon's bind.

docs/CONFIGURATION.md and docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md describe the Origin rule and the WSL bind, task fields carry no exploit walkthrough, and `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` plus `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
LIVE WSL CHECK, end to end, in scratch only, for DoD 1 and DoD 2 on a real Windows host. Never touch the live daemon (port 9876), the repo's .moe/ or the shared node_modules.

1. Snapshot.
   - `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh scratch dir on D: (Windows-visible), e.g. /mnt/d/projexts/moe-wslcheck-<utc>/repo.
   - Through cmd.exe and the Windows node, run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` then `npm run build` in its packages/moe-daemon.
2. Scratch project: an empty directory beside it, initialised with that dist's init or start. Start it with PowerShell `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`, so it outlives the interop console:
   `<Windows node> <snap>\packages\moe-daemon\dist\index.js start --project <scratch project> --port 9990 --host wsl`
   Wait for its daemon.json to appear.
3. Bind proof (Windows): `cmd.exe /d /c "netstat -ano -p TCP | findstr :9990"` lists 127.0.0.1:9990, plus the WSL adapter address when one exists, and NEVER 0.0.0.0:9990. The scratch daemon.json records bindHost 'wsl'.
4. Discovery proof (from WSL). Use moe-agent.sh's own candidate order and probe commands: read probe_daemon_health and wsl_gateway_host, and reuse their exact commands. MOE_DAEMON_HOST must be unset, then try 127.0.0.1, then the WSL gateway.
   - The first candidate that answers serves /health with status healthy.
   - On that same host, a curl WebSocket upgrade to /mcp (HTTP/1.1, Upgrade, Connection, Sec-WebSocket-Version 13, a random Sec-WebSocket-Key) gets 101.
   - The same upgrade with an Origin header gets 403.
   - Record which candidate answered (mirrored or NAT).
5. Teardown, always, even on failure:
   - run `<snap>\packages\moe-daemon\dist\index.js stop --project <scratch project>`;
   - confirm netstat no longer lists :9990;
   - delete the scratch directories.

Error handling:
- If the Windows node or npm is missing, or the firewall blocks every candidate, record the exact command, exit code and output in the step note, and report it in complete_task as not proven. Never claim it passed.
- Use a fixed port 9990, and refuse to start if :9990 is already listening.
